name: Jihoon Lee
role: Ph.D. Student in Electrical & Electronic Engineering
intro: I study how wireless networks can support reliable coordination and intelligent services. My research spans vehicle-to-everything communication, 6G beam management, and semantic communication.
about: I am a Ph.D. student at Yonsei University, advised by Prof. Seong-Lyun Kim in the Robotic and Mobile Networks Laboratory. I combine analytical modeling, algorithm design, and system-level simulation to study communication under mobility and uncertainty. My recent interests include reliable token transmission and the integration of AI services with virtualized radio access networks.

research.label: Connected mobility
research.title: Coordinating vehicles over the air.
research.description: Joint communication and control for vehicle platoons. AirCons exploits wireless signal superposition to share aggregate state information without individual channel-state feedback.

research.label: 6G air interface
research.title: Keeping beams aligned in motion.
research.description: Position-aware MAC design and stochastic-geometry analysis of beam misalignment, with a focus on access probability, beamwidth, and the trade-off between alignment overhead and throughput.

research.label: Semantic communication
research.title: Protecting meaning, beyond bits.
research.description: Semantic-similarity-based token clustering, bit mapping, and power allocation for reliable communication over noisy channels. I also explore the interaction between AI inference and radio access networks.
